title: Complete proof of Erdős Problem #1095: The Erdős-Selfridge Function

problemStatement.plain: Formal investigation in number theory: Complete proof of Erdős Problem #1095: The Erdős-Selfridge Function.

knowledge.progressSummary: SURVEYED: 3 sorries (1 unique), 10 axioms. Core blocker is existence proof for g(k). Simple witness fails; needs Ecklund-Erdos-Selfridge 1974 argument.
insights: Core issue: g(k) definition uses sorry in Nat.find existence proof
Need to show: ∃ n > k+1, all prime factors of C(n,k) > k
Simple witness k!+k+1 does NOT obviously work (C(p,k) can have small factors)
Ecklund-Erdos-Selfridge 1974 proved existence, but the proof is non-trivial
10 axioms: 5 deep bounds (EES, Konyagin, LCM, ELS), 5 concrete values (g(2)=3,...,g(6)=143)
Concrete values g(2)=3, g(3)=7 are verifiable: C(3,2)=3 (only factor 3>2), C(7,3)=35=5*7 (both>3)
The 3 sorries are actually 1 sorry repeated 3 times (same existence proof)
Fix priority: prove existence → this eliminates all 3 sorries at once
nextSteps: Research Ecklund-Erdos-Selfridge 1974 existence proof for g(k)
Alternative: prove existence via Chinese Remainder Theorem (find n ≡ 1 mod each prime ≤ k)
Once existence proved: g(2)..g(6) values might be provable by native_decide
